The specific name refers to the diminutive frons of the soldier.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: head in dorsal view almost black on the anterior 2/3, rusty on the posterior 1/3; the median notch of the frontal margin with characteristic zipper-like alternating corrugations; frontal face deeply concave, meeting the vertex face at 70°; genal horns almost absent; mandibles very short, without a swelling; antennae 11—13-segmented, mostly 12; the first marginal tooth of each mandible very short and blunt. Alate: antennae 15—17-segmented, mostly 16, segment formula 2>3=4=5; pronotum about as wide as the head (including the compound eyes), wider than long. Closest to C. rotundiceps, which is distinctly larger and in which the median notch of the frontal margin is weak or lacks corrugations.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body pale brown. Frontal face pale yellow-brown, vertex pale brown. The darkest pigment lies on the wing scales, forming a central brown chevron mark; wing membrane pale brown, the sclerotized veins brown. Labrum very pale yellow-brown. Pronotum and antennae pale brown. Pronotum with a cross-shaped mark formed by very pale brown bands and a white midline. Abdominal tergites pale brown, sternites very pale brown. Legs very pale brown to pale brown. Head subsquare, the cranial sutures almost invisible. Compound eyes oval, medium-sized. Ocelli oval, touching the compound eyes. Antennae 15—17-segmented, mostly 16, segment formula 2>3=4=5. Pronotum about as wide as the head (including the compound eyes), wider than long, the sides slightly convex; anterior margin slightly concave, posterior margin slightly emarginate. Radial vein of the forewing reaching 1/4 of the wing length from the wing base; radial sector with 6—8 branches. Arolia present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head in dorsal view almost black on the anterior 2/3, rusty on the posterior 1/3; in lateral view nearly black on the anterior 2/3, rusty orange on the posterior 1/3 (around the foramen magnum). Mandibles chestnut brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum with a rusty orange bow-tie-shaped mark, the remainder pale yellow. Head in dorsal view with the sides parallel or slightly divergent anteriorly; posterior corners broadly rounded, posterior margin almost straight; anterior outline slightly bracket-shaped. Middle of the vertex slightly concave. Head capsule sculpture widespread, dense, shallow and almost uniform, smoother at the middle of the vertex in some specimens. Frontal margin most prominent in frontal view; broadly concave, clearly delimited from the vertex; median notch with alternating zipper-like corrugations; the margin almost smooth but dull; distinctly rounded in cross-section. Frontal face deeply concave, with a small flat median area, meeting the clypeus at almost a right angle; the frontal face textured but shining. Frontal face meeting the vertex face at 70°. Labrum blunt, swollen at the apex, very weakly truncate laterally. Frontal horns stout, vertical, slightly narrower than long, separated from both the frontal margin and the clypeus; directed forward or slightly outward. Genal horns almost absent. Mandibles very short, without a swelling, angled; horizontal in lateral view; the first marginal tooth of each mandible very short and blunt. Compound eyes small, oval, when visible. Antennae 11—13-segmented, mostly 12, segment formula 2>3=4=5 or 2>3>4=5. Pronotum subsquare, the anterior margin shallowly notched, the posterior margin almost straight, the sides convex; anterior margin densely covered with blunt undulations. Comparison with C. rotundiceps: in the present species the median notch of the frontal margin bears zipper-like alternating corrugations, whereas in C. rotundiceps the notch is weak or absent and lacks corrugations; the latter has still shorter mandibles and a larger body.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Distribution: Lesser Antilles — mainland Trinidad (including Chacachacare and Monos islands) and Grenada; not known elsewhere. Uncommon on mainland Trinidad, apparently more abundant on Grenada and on the islands northwest of Trinidad. Geographic variation: the frontal concavity is shallower in specimens from Grenada. Type locality: William's Bay, Diego Martin, Trinidad and Tobago.
